clue.text: With British numbers game you may end up loaded

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance played by matching drawn numbers, like bingo

explanation.surface: A Brit who plays a numbers game might end up rich, loaded with winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' seems to mean wealthy after a lottery win, but here it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very drunk, the same state as being plastered or sozzled.

clue.text: Flower that lacks colour, initially, like 29

definitions.note: 29-across is FLATTER, a verb; the answer is a phrasal verb of the same meaning

indicators.note: a flower that lacks something has a letter taken away from it

parts.note: the buttercup is a common yellow meadow flower

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word colour

explanation.surface: A pale flower missing its colour is compared to something else in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like 29' points to 29-across, so the answer means much the same as that verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To butter someone up is to praise them insincerely, the same as to sweet-talk them.

clue.text: Tread lightly in this tricky situation

definitions.text: Tread lightly in this tricky situation

parts.words: Tread lightly in this tricky situation
parts.note: pictures skating carefully over a thin frozen surface, which is also an idiom for a precarious position

explanation.surface: Advice to step carefully when things get delicate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being in a risky position, as a skater on a fragile frozen pond literally is.

clue.text: Bite made by climbing insect

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word for the insect reads upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: a gnat is a small biting fly

explanation.surface: A bite delivered by an insect crawling upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bite here means a sharp flavour, a zest or piquancy on the tongue.

clue.text: Tripe and nuts wanted for urban revelry?

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the preceding words go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone wants tripe and nuts as food before a night out in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like a food beside tripe but is the anagram signal for TRIPE AND. The definition alludes to the phrase 'paint the town red', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint the town red is to celebrate wildly on a night out, so the phrase hints at city carousing.

clue.text: Teacher shows English coin of old gold

parts.note: the ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in past centuries
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A teacher displays an antique English gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry, a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is someone who instructs, a schoolmaster or tutor.

clue.text: Pernickety individual

definitions.meaning: fussy and hard to please about details
relating to one specific item rather than to a group

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fussy about details and specific to one single case.

clue.text: I finally won and took gold

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word won

parts.note: took and got both mean obtained

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that at last they triumphed and walked off with the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold' is the definition: a bar of cast gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast block of metal, typically a bar of gold bullion.

clue.text: Giants — there's one in No 10!

definitions.meaning: huge, powerful beings, as in Greek myth
the answer to 10-across contains one of these mythical giants within its spelling

explanation.surface: Big figures, one of whom resides at the Prime Minister's address.
explanation.walkthrough: No 10 suggests Downing Street, but it points to 10-across, whose first five letters spell a single giant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were the race of giant gods who preceded the Olympians.

clue.text: Clear the wine cellar

definitions.meaning: to clear an obstacle is to leap over it
an underground room for storing wine

explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap over an obstacle, and a vault is also an arched cellar for storing wine.

clue.text: Liner nearly given a queen's name

indicators.note: nearly means the name of the liner stops one letter short

parts.note: the Titanic was the famous ocean liner that sank in 1912

explanation.surface: A ship is almost given the name of a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' drops the final C of TITANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Titania is queen of the fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Honourable post

definitions.meaning: decent and of strict moral integrity
a vertical pole or support

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both morally decent and, as a noun, a vertical supporting pole.

clue.text: Unfinished piece adapted for major work

indicators.note: adapted means the remaining letters are altered into a new order
unfinished means the word piece loses its final letter

explanation.surface: An incomplete piece of writing is reworked into a major opus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims PIECE to PIEC, and 'adapted' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, ambitious work such as a heroic poem or sweeping film.

clue.text: Run off with a bird, we're told, like a dirty dog

indicators.note: we're told means the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: to run off is to flee; the bittern is a wading bird of the heron family

explanation.surface: A dog bolts after a bird, and it is described as mucky.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud in a non-rhotic British accent, FLEE BITTERN sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog infested with fleas and their bites is shabby and scruffy.

clue.text: Where members appreciate good service

parts.note: reads like a restaurant or club praising its staff, but service is the opening stroke in a racket sport

explanation.surface: A members' establishment that values attentive staff.
explanation.definitionFit: At a club for a racket sport, members admire a strong serve that starts each point.

clue.text: Could be your team's in agreement

definitions.meaning: many football clubs have this word in their names, such as Manchester or Leeds
joined together and of one mind

explanation.surface: Your sports side might be in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is part of many football club names, and also means joined in harmony.

clue.text: Body parts keeping us in extra cash

indicators.note: keeping means the word for body parts holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: bones are parts of the body's skeleton

explanation.surface: Body parts hold on to the people getting additional pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals a container; 'in' is only a link word, not a second insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonuses are extra payments on top of normal wages.

clue.text: American helicopter kept in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: US slang for a rotary-winged aircraft, from the whirling blades
a utensil for whisking

explanation.definitionFit: It is US slang for a chopper, and also a hand whisk stored with cooking utensils.

clue.text: Clive: run out! it caused a deafening roar

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Clive is run out and the crowd roars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run out' looks like a cricket dismissal, but 'run' is fodder with CLIVE and 'out' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A culverin was an early cannon, whose firing made a thunderous noise.

clue.text: Decrepit aircraft like 4, full of holes

parts.note: a crate is slang for an old, rickety plane or car
4-across is red paint, so the colour is the shade meant

explanation.surface: An old plane painted like 4 is riddled with holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cratered describes ground pitted with hollows, as from bombs or meteors.

clue.text: English and French pronouns can be really awful

parts.note: he is an English pronoun
I is another English pronoun
nous is the French pronoun meaning we

explanation.surface: Mixing English and French pronouns can be dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: HE and I are English pronouns, NOUS (we) is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinous means wicked or atrocious, deserving utter condemnation.

clue.text: Fancy German eating place

indicators.note: fancy implies something elaborate or fanciful, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fancy German restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' seems to describe the restaurant, but rearranges GERMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A manger is a trough from which livestock feed.

clue.text: What you can do with 4, cause trouble

definitions.meaning: 4-across is red paint, which you mix with a stick before use
to make mischief and provoke discord

explanation.definitionFit: One mixes a tin of paint with a stick, and the idiom means stoking discord.

clue.text: Join university faculty without a religion

indicators.note: without means the following letters are removed from the word faculty

parts.note: a cult is a religious sect

explanation.surface: Someone joins a university department that lacks any faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes A and CULT from FACULTY, leaving FY.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring together into one whole, to combine.

clue.text: Sort of negativism designed to speed things up

indicators.note: sort here means to arrange, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of pessimism devised to hurry things along.
explanation.definitionFit: Something time-saving reduces the time a task takes, making it quicker.

clue.text: Transport check to illustrate "Safety First", say

parts.note: the MOT is the compulsory annual roadworthiness test for vehicles in Britain

explanation.surface: A vehicle inspection showcases a road safety slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's yearly road-safety test for cars, from the old Ministry of Transport.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan like that is a guiding maxim or watchword.

clue.text: Questions for 27, possibly

definitions.meaning: an examination of set questions
27-down is GAME; a ... match is an international cricket game

explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a match between national cricket teams, so it is one kind of 27.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a set of questions, and a Test is an international cricket match.

clue.text: Willing old maid is an example to us

definitions.meaning: ready and eager to take part
old maid is a children's card ...

explanation.definitionFit: Being up for something means willing, and old maid is a card pastime.

clue.text: Baby's toy right to be viewed as potential killer

parts.note: a rattle is a noisy toy for a baby

explanation.surface: A baby's toy might seem dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattler is short for rattlesnake, a venomous snake whose bite can be deadly.

clue.text: Smoother compliment

definitions.meaning: more level and even
as a verb, to praise someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means more level, and also to praise someone to please them.

clue.text: Instrument supplied when gypsy tucks into large steak

indicators.note: tucks into suggests one piece is placed inside another, the gypsy going into the steak

parts.note: a T-bone is a big cut of beef with a T-shaped bone
a Rom is a member of the Romani people

explanation.surface: An instrument is provided when a traveller eats a large steak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like eating the steak, but it signals one piece going inside the other. 'Gypsy' for a Romani person is dated usage common in older crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A trombone is a brass instrument with a sliding tube.

clue.text: Get angry — after using 4 you would

definitions.meaning: to become furious
4-across is red paint; after using it the colour is all you would perceive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper, and literally after painting you would view that colour.
